description.narrative: Increased livestock sales from sustainable smallholder production in the project areas.

50% of fresh pork and beef available in Luang Prabang and Phonsavanh (Xienkhoung) towns butchered at HACCP-certified facilities (baseline 2014: 0%) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Not achieved. The pig population in Lao PDR was severely affected by the African Swine Fever pandemic from June 2019 onwards. Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System National livestock Census Annual trade statistics Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

On average, SLPMG members sell heavier live animals: pigs: 55 kg (baseline 2014: 45 kg) and cattle: 225 kg (baseline 2014: 200 kg); and sell more animals with increased annual sales of pigs: 18 (baseline 2014: 12) and cattle: 5 (baseline 2014: 3) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The impact indicator - increase in incomes of targeted livestock producers - has been far exceeded, with the actual 2020 average income level (LAK 25.6m per household) over three times the 2026 DMF target (LAK 8.0m per household); this can be attributed largely to an increase in livestock output prices. This proves that investment in livestock production is an effective strategy for rural poverty reduction.
Achieved. On average, pigs weighed 70 kg.
Achieved. On average, cattle weighed 262 kg.
Not achieved. On average, 9 pigs per smallholder farm were sold.
Partially achieved. On average, 3.8 cattle per smallholder farm were so Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System National livestock Census Annual trade statistics Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Output: 1. Strengthened capacities of smallholders and other livestock value chain actors. Indicator: 55 traders trained in OIE standards Achievement: 30 Progress/Status: Achieved. 314 traders trained in OIE standards, 129 women (41%) Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System

Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System

Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System

Output: 1. Strengthened capacities of smallholders and other livestock value chain actors. Indicator: 85 trained students participate in the internship program in project villages (20% female) Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Achieved. 101 students of which 50, or 49.5% were women) in the internship program to neighboring districts to learn and share experiences. Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System

Output: 1. Strengthened capacities of smallholders and other livestock value chain actors. Indicator: Five policy support studies completed with policy documents and associated regulations drafted Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Achieved. Output: 1. Strengthened capacities of smallholders and other livestock value chain actors. Indicator: One new course on animal butchering and meat processing established in NAFC Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Achieved. Academic diploma program established at NAFC, includes 5 meat and butcher vocational courses and 14 academic subjects. Data Source: Project Benefit Monitoring System

Output: 2. Livestock value chain infrastructure strengthened Indicator: Two demonstration slaughterhouses and one meat processing facility managed and operating with HACCP certification (separate toilets for men and women) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. One slaughterhouse in Xieng Khouang and one meat processing training facility at NAFC completed, equipped with separate toilets for men and women. in January 2023. The other planned slaughterhouse at Luang Prabang was not completed. Data Source: Project Performance Management System
